hook: California Hall, built in 1912 as the German House and the social center of the city's German community until 1984.

parcel.note: Institutional addresses are usually deferred on this site; this page exists because the address was named in the prompting source. The parcel spans 601, 605 and 625 Polk Street, and DBI files permits under 601, 605 and 625.
parcel.address_note: Issue #19 gives the German House's address as 624 Polk Street. 624 Polk is parcel 0741006B on the west side of the street — the Mayfair Hotel of 1928, per SF Planning — and cannot be the building the same entry describes. The cornerstone ceremony it records at Polk and Turk, the five storeys, the 1912 completion and the landmark designation all match 0742002, which SF Planning names CALIFORNIA HALL and dates to 1912.

historic_status.reason: Article 10 Individual Landmark, Historic Survey Result

historic_district.note: The parcel's coordinates fall inside no historic district; its protection is the individual Article 10 designation.

permits.description: Permit to legalize the existing post-secondary educational institution use at 601–625 Polk under planning case 2008.0586, with no change of use proposed, plus security camera repairs.
A Caltrans 1-A pole foundation installed over the existing sub-sidewalk basement.
Re-roofing — the existing built-up roof removed, the concrete inspected, and a twenty-year single-ply roof laid.
Fire sprinklers installed for the fourth-floor teaching kitchens, with the electrical, plumbing, mechanical and hood work under separate permits.
A lecture room remodelled into a teaching kitchen and demonstration lecture room, and the basement corridor remodelled.
Lecture rooms on the third and fourth floors remodelled into teaching kitchens and demonstration lecture rooms, one on each floor.
Additions and alterations to the fifth floor of California Hall.
New restrooms, and doors for partitions.
An enclosure built to support an electrical transformer.

permit_summary.note: Nine of the 147 filings on this parcel are shown — the largest by stated cost, plus the earliest on file. The rest are sprinkler, fire-alarm and hood permits from the culinary-academy fit-out, renewals of expired permits for final inspection, and sign and street-space permits.

historical_record.description: The German House was completed, following a cornerstone-laying ceremony at Polk and Turk Streets attended by German Consul General Bopp, Mayor James Rolph and Governor Hiram Johnson.

historical_record.summary: Social center of the German community
historical_record.description: The German House was the social center of San Francisco's German community, housing dozens of clubs and societies.
The Club Puertorriqueño de San Francisco held events in California Hall through the 1960s and 1970s.

California Hall, a designated San Francisco landmark (No. 174); the Daughters of Bilitis held their first public event here in April 1956, and on 1 January 1965 the New Year's Mardi Gras Ball held here for the Council on Religion and the Homosexual was met by police with floodlights and cameras, an episode that turned clergy and lawyers into public allies of the city's homophile organisations.

historical_record.summary: Sold and converted to a culinary academy
historical_record.description: The building was sold and converted to a culinary academy.
The Metropolitan Community Church, the second-oldest LGBTQ congregation in the United States, held its services at California Hall here in 1970 and 1971.
